answer: To stem the rising tide of sybil attacks, an agent economy can enforce non-refundable proof-of-burn entry fees for every new digital identity. When a malicious actor attempts to mirror their operations across thousands of fake personas, this protocol requires permanently destroying scarce native tokens in the sable depths of an unspendable null address. Because spawning each new node imposes an irreversible and compounding financial loss, the attacker's capital is swiftly exhausted, rendering mass identity manipulation economically ruinous.
